    def _training_partition(self, ids, offsets, owners):
        # Packed histories are already binary and deduplicated. Randomly order
        # items within each row using the main process's Torch training stream.
        lengths = offsets[1:] - offsets[:-1]
        permutation = torch.rand(ids.numel(), device=ids.device).argsort()
        permutation = permutation[
            torch.argsort(owners[permutation], stable=True)]
        within_row = torch.arange(ids.numel(), device=ids.device) - (
            offsets[owners[permutation]])
        withheld = torch.zeros_like(ids, dtype=torch.bool)
        withheld[permutation] = within_row < (lengths[owners[permutation]] // 2)
        context = ~withheld
        # Singleton rows reconstruct their sole item from that same item.
        targets = withheld | lengths[owners].eq(1)
        context_lengths = lengths - lengths // 2
        context_offsets = torch.cat([
            offsets.new_zeros(1), context_lengths.cumsum(0)])
        return ids[context], context_offsets, ids[targets], owners[targets]

    def forward(self, ids, offsets, owners, anneal):
        if self.training:
            context_ids, context_offsets, target_ids, target_owners = (
                self._training_partition(ids, offsets, owners))
        else:
            context_ids, context_offsets = ids, offsets
            target_ids, target_owners = ids, owners
        h, mu, logvar = self.representation(context_ids, context_offsets)
